subject: Animation
title: Émile Cohl: The Father of Animated Film
description: One-minute skill: Émile Cohl: The Father of Animated Film.

hook.text: In 1908, French artist Émile Cohl drew 700 images and filmed them to create the first true animated cartoon.

buildup.text: His film Fantasmagorie showed stick figures morphing and transforming in a two-minute stream of imagination.

discovery.text: Cohl drew each frame on paper, then photographed them against a lit surface to create the moving image.

twist.text: Cohl died in poverty in 1938. He never profited from inventing an art form worth billions today.

climax.text: Fantasmagorie established the core principles of frame-by-frame animation that the entire industry still uses.

punchline.text: Seven hundred drawings invented a billion-dollar art form.

quiz.question: Why is Émile Cohl considered the father of animated film?
options: He created Fantasmagorie in 1908, the first true animated cartoon using frame-by-frame drawing
He founded the first animation studio

details.summary: Émile Cohl created Fantasmagorie in 1908, widely considered the first fully animated film. The French caricaturist drew 700 images to create two minutes of surreal, morphing line animation that launched the animated film medium.
details.whyItMatters: Cohl's Fantasmagorie established that drawings could tell stories through continuous movement on screen. His work marks the true beginning of animated cinema, predating the more famous American pioneers by several years.
takeaways: Fantasmagorie in 1908 is considered the first fully animated film
Cohl drew 700 individual images for two minutes of animation
His surreal, morphing style influenced experimental animation for decades

faq.question: What makes Fantasmagorie the first animated film?
faq.answer: While earlier films used animation techniques, Fantasmagorie was the first to consist entirely of animated drawings telling a continuous, character-driven story. Each frame was drawn separately on paper, photographed, and projected as a seamless sequence.

faq.question: Why is Émile Cohl less famous than later animation pioneers?
faq.answer: Cohl worked before animation became an industry and died in poverty. American animators like Disney built commercial empires that preserved their legacy, while Cohl's pioneering work remained obscure outside film history circles.
